research_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — selected building kept separate from the campus
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: IM3 inventory geometry and provenance; Markley current and archived operator pages; Lowell assessor parcel P90290/MBLU 184/4765/2; 2015, 2018, 2020, 2023 and 2024 City planning and bond records; deed/sale fields; and web archives. Exact identifiers included 2 Prince Avenue, 1 Markley Way, parcel 184/4765/2, assessor pid 47203 and IM3 source record 00214321737. The evidence supports a June 2015 purchase, Phase One open with customer occupancy by November 23, 2015, a three-building 14.4-acre assessor parcel, a later 65,000-square-foot expansion approval and continuing equipment changes. It does not map the selected 123,665-square-foot inventory footprint to an assessor building number or allocate campus investment, jobs, capacity, incentives or current white space to that polygon.

source.title: Thanksgiving Reflection: Top 3 Things Markley Group is Thankful for in 2015
source.notes: The operator reported that Phase One of its 350,000-square-foot Lowell facility had opened and that customers had begun occupying space by November 23, 2015. This is an operating-no-later-than anchor for Phase One, not a commissioning date for every building or later expansion.

research_updates.title: Investment, incentive and fiscal audit — forecasts separated from cumulative observations
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: the 2015 EACC approval release; City TIF summaries and FY2020-FY2026 budgets; the 2023 preliminary official statement; EDIP awardee, annual-report, compliance and decertification pages; City Council packets; assessor history; and the Treasurer/Collector billing portal. FY2020 records the agreement as executed in May 2015, and the 2017 City summary describes a clawback provision and Middlesex 3 membership requirement; the signed agreement itself was not located. The fragment retains the $72.8 million Phase I plan, $104,121,860 cumulative-investment observation, $77,182,505 combined local incentive forecast, $187,500 approved state credit, $1,624,655.79 cumulative real-estate TIF savings and a separate $534,231.97 FY2026 real-property bill. Exact searches of adopted-budget documents 20496 (FY2023), 23767 (FY2024), 26555 (FY2025) and 30950 (FY2026 proposed) found no Markley row, and no 2021-2024 annual certified-employment table surfaced. The four FY2026 InvoiceCloud quarters are complete and show zero balances, but billed tax is not cash received and the portal does not identify adjustment versus payment. Partial FY2025/FY2027 displays are excluded; personal-property search returned no open Markley invoice and does not establish historical exemption value. The sources do not reconcile proposal vintages, prove credit use, publish annual realized abatements, allocate tax among jurisdictions, quantify public-service cost or support a net fiscal result.

source.title: City of Lowell InvoiceCloud real-estate tax lookup — parcel P90290
source.notes: Interactive real-estate search by parcel ID P90290 returned all four FY2026 quarterly invoices: 2026reQ100014595 ($58,150.30), 2026reQ200014595 ($58,150.29), 2026reQ300014595 ($208,965.69) and 2026reQ400014595 ($208,965.69), each with zero balance. The same current-results page displayed only partial FY2025 and FY2027 sets, which are excluded. Bill total is not cash received, and zero balance does not distinguish payment from adjustment or abatement. A personal-property search for owner MARKLEY returned no open invoices; that result cannot establish historical liability or exemption value.

research_updates.title: Assessor and parcel audit — four annual real-property stocks added
research_updates.notes: The official Vision Government Solutions Lowell portal was searched by Markley, Prince Avenue, Markley Way, parcel ID P90290, MBLU 184/4765/2 and property-record pid 47203. The card identifies Markley Group LLC, three buildings, 14.4 acres, a $3.85 million June 15, 2015 sale, and 2023-2026 total parcel values. The four total values are retained as one whole-parcel annual series. The sale price is not forced into an investment metric, individual building replacement-cost fields are not summed as economic activity, the 2026 value jump is not labeled new investment, and no selected-building, personal-property, payment or jurisdictional-distribution series was available from the card. The separate Treasurer/Collector portal supplies one complete real-property billing year and is not treated as an assessor value or cash receipt.

source.title: Lowell property record card — parcel 184/4765/2, 2 Prince Avenue
source.notes: The official property card identifies owner Markley Group LLC, parcel ID P90290/MBLU 184/4765/2, 14.4 acres, three buildings and a June 15, 2015 sale for $3.85 million. Its valuation history reports total real-property values of $9,766,900 for 2023, $10,050,800 for 2024, $10,144,300 for 2025 and $24,239,200 for 2026. Building living areas sum to 307,030 square feet, which is not reconciled to the operator's differently defined 352,000 square feet of secured white space or to the selected IM3 footprint.

research_updates.title: Construction, suppliers and procurement audit — five issued permit values added without aggregation
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Lowell Planning Board applications, memoranda, plans and minutes; the public monthly issued-permit indexes for 2024, 2025 and January-June 2026; City online-permitting guidance; contractor and engineer portfolios; COMMBUYS and Massachusetts statewide IT contract records; tenant procurement disclosures; and archived trade coverage for 2015-2026. The City reports BLD202400574 at $3,350,000, ELC202406426 at $4,000,000, BLD202413857 at $15,538,186, ELC202507553 at $12,717,600 and BLD202603584 at $1,708,090. Each is retained once at its issue year even when later monthly reports repeat it as year-to-date or completion activity; related building, foundation and trade permits are not summed because scope overlap is unresolved. Exact searches of the relevant official reports did not locate third-party-cited ELC202409585, so its $19,076,500 figure is excluded. Named roles include Willard L. Cleveland, New England Electric Group and Markley Group Boston; the older contractor case study separately identifies Coordinated Systems Consulting and Saiful Bouquet. The CSS portal requires a registered login and the City page reports online permitting unavailable. No final contract amount, invoice, audited annual outlay, equipment-versus-building split, construction headcount, worker hours, payroll, residence, vendor payment or local-purchase share was found. Permit values are administrative estimates, not cash spending.

source.title: City of Lowell permits issued analysis — August 2025
source.notes: Page 1675 identifies ELC202507553, issued June 17, 2025, with estimated cost $12,717,600 for four switchgear rooms, four generators, eight PDU units, four chiller units, eight load centers and miscellaneous electrical work; New England Electric Group is the electrical contractor. The same report lists other Markley building, foundation, plumbing and electrical permits, but potentially overlapping trade scopes are not summed.

research_updates.title: Operations and workforce audit — dated headcounts and local-resident subset added
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: Lowell TIF tables and annual certified-project reports; Massachusetts EDIP annual-report, compliance and decertification material; Markley careers, staff and facility pages; job boards; customer and tenant records; workforce-development, apprenticeship, local-hiring and wage-enforcement searches; and state procurement records for 2015-2026. Exact City/EDIP searches found dated Markley rows for 2019, December 2020 and December 31, 2025 but no public 2021-2024 annual certified-employment table. The account retains 26 employees in 2019, 31 in December 2020 and 101 full-time permanent employees at the Lowell location on December 31, 2025, including a non-additive subset of 30 Lowell residents. The 2025 report also lists 29 hires during that year, but the available metric is a stock and the hire flow stays in source metadata. The State ITS86 listing makes Markley Boston LLC contract-eligible and states a supplier-diversity commitment, but it does not disclose a Lowell-facility procurement payment and contributes no amount. No annual-average FTE, occupation table, wage, payroll, hours, apprenticeship outcome, contractor/customer headcount, turnover, county-resident total, procurement payment or selected-building employment was found.

source.title: Lowell City Council March 10, 2026 packet — 2025 certified-project employment report
source.notes: The certified-project table, sourced to the Massachusetts Office of Business Development/EDIP annual report dated December 31, 2025, reports 101 full-time permanent employees at Markley's Lowell location, 29 hires during 2025, and 30 employees living in Lowell. The total and resident subset are retained as separate stocks; the 29 hires are not forced into the stock metric.

research_updates.title: Resource, utility and environmental audit — permit equipment added; consumption remains unallocated
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: MassDEP air-plan applications, notices and OADR decisions under 24-AQ02F-0001-APP/NE-25-002, including the March 27, 2026 final decision and July 2026 reconsideration docket; Lowell Planning Board, Sustainability Council, water, sewer and data-center materials; fuel-storage licensing; National Grid and Massachusetts DPU dockets and tariffs; ISO New England queue and reliability material; EPA facility searches; Markley facility, PPA and sustainability pages; and 2025-2026 reporting based on water bills or operator statements. The permit-listed facility total of 27 emergency generators is retained, distinct from installation and operation. The City authorized four 6,000-gallon diesel tanks in July 2025; a later fuel-license amendment application filed September 8 was withdrawn October 13, so no additional capacity is inferred. Licensed tank capacity is not fuel inventory or use and the vocabulary has no matching storage-capacity metric. AP reports an operator-stated summer peak of about 118,000 gallons per day, but no meter ledger or annual total was published and the vocabulary has no direct actual peak-water metric. A Markley solar PPA covers a broader company purchase in Eversource territory and is not allocated to the National Grid-served Lowell site. No facility annual electricity, demand, tariff payment, grid-upgrade cost, verified annual water/wastewater, generator runtime, fuel use, actual emissions or selected-building resource series was found.

source.title: In the Matter of Markley Group, LLC — Recommended Final Decision, OADR 2025-022
source.notes: Page 2 says Air Quality Plan Approval NE-25-002 authorized eight additional diesel emergency generators, bringing the permit-listed facility total to 27, for an expansion intended to serve increased AI use. The MassDEP Commissioner adopted the recommended decision on March 27, 2026. Authorization is not proof that every generator was installed or operated and does not establish runtime, generation, fuel use, emissions or public cost.

research_updates.title: Community-recipient audit — one recipient-verified Lowell contribution added
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: University of Massachusetts Lowell, Middlesex Community College, Greater Lowell Community Foundation, Lowell Public Schools, youth sports, libraries, housing and food-assistance recipients; City packets; Markley press and social pages; and local news archives for grants, sponsorships, donations, STEM, education and volunteer support from 2015-2026. UMass Lowell lists Markley Group in the $25,000 Signature Sponsor tier for the Meehan Student Center dedication held May 1-2, 2026, providing a dated recipient-side amount. The University says the weekend raised more than $300,000 in total, but that event total is not attributed to Markley. Operator-side references to other local sponsorships and aggregate giving lacked matching recipient ledgers or defensible facility allocation and are not combined. No complete annual Middlesex County grant register, in-kind valuation, volunteer-hour series or campus-attributable community total was found.

source.title: Meehan Student Center dedication — Thank You to Our Sponsors
source.notes: The recipient page lists Markley Group in the Signature Sponsor tier of $25,000 for the Meehan Student Center dedication. The contribution is a company/county community transfer, not a recurring annual amount, campus operating expense, tax payment or proof of a complete local-giving ledger.

research_updates.title: Structured-data and modeling audit — no defensible residual or county-effect model
research_updates.notes: Repository county economic panels for 2001-2024, study-county exclusions, inventory history and the direct evidence documented above were reviewed. The November 2015 operating anchor leaves a pre-period, but Markley is not Middlesex County's first known data-center operation: the repository's governed first-entry research documents earlier colocation activity in Somerville, and Markley itself had later 2018-2026 expansions that prevent a single stable treatment boundary. Newly retained permit estimates do not supply audited spending, labor coefficients or local-purchase shares, and the FY2026 billed-tax record has no same-scope marginal public-service cost. No project-specific construction payroll, supplier spending, operating payroll, annual resource quantity compatible with the evidence metrics or causal county outcome anchors were found. No construction, supplier, household, resource, fiscal-net, input-output, difference-in-differences, event-study, synthetic-control or descriptive county-comparison model is added; arbitrary transferred assumptions would create false precision rather than a bounded estimate. No records requests were made.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project.
